To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hydrostatic work pressure does not affect the methane production rate and the methane yield, as the pressure does not affect neither the methane producing bacteria, nor the methane consuming bacteria.
the methane producing bacteria have an optimum pressure range of 1.0-2.0 bar.
methane-producing bacteria are sensitive to the pressure, but their proliferation is not affected by pressure in the range of 0.5 to 3.0 MPa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the work pressure on the methane production rate and on the methane yield for the organic substrates used in anaerobic digestion.
the influence of the pressure in anaerobe fermentation on methane-producing bacteria and their activity in the biogas process.
the influence of pressure on methanogens loading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the hydrostatic pressure is not a negative factor in the process of anaerobic digestion.
the hydrostatic pressures up to 10 MPa are not negatively influencing on the methanogens activity and the biogas producing processes.
the pressure effects are negligible and the hydrostatic pressure is not a limiting factor in the anaerobic digestion process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrostatic pressures in the anaerobic digestors are likely to influence the methanogenic microorganisms in the bioreactor and consequently on the efficiency of the biogases production.
the methanogens proliferation is negatively influenced by the hydrostatic pressure and that this influence is more pronounced in case of high methane producing slurry.
the hydrostatic pressures up to 10 bar have no influence on the proliferation of the methane-producing bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the methane production is not affected by pressure.
the pressure has no influence on the proliferation of the methanogen bacteria, and consequently, the pressure does not affect the biogas yield.
the methanogens proliferation is influenced by the hydrostatic pressure, but in a different manner, depending on the type of the methanogen.
